@carlosantoniodasilva Any updates on this issue? It seems I have the same problem...

From what I see, it seems that the issue has to do with the way Rails handles transactions.
When `ActiveRecord::Rollback` is raised it is rescued silently by the closest transaction block. However since in case of dependent destroy the two transaction blocks (initial destroy, and dependent destroy) the exception is rescued  from the inner transaction block and the rollback never happens (for details on this one you can check the section Nested Transactions in http://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/Transactions/ClassMethods.html). I am not sure if it is an easy fix, but it seems that the solution should be to re-raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback` transactions in case the transaction block is running within another block. /cc @carlosantoniodasilva
